title: Slice-Aware Quantization Risk Mitigation Manifest
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview
========
This document defines a slice-aware risk assessment and mitigation manifest for applying aggressive quantization profiles to production models. It is intended for model owners, inference engineers, and oncall responders responsible for model promotion into Dedicated/Private deployments and for hosted inference rollouts. The goal is to reduce token cost through quantization while bounding downstream quality regressions by model slice, with clear monitoring, canarying, and rollback rules.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all model promotions where a quantized artifact (INT8/FP16/mixed) is used in production inference.
- Focuses on per-slice risk (user cohorts, prompt families, long-context windows, function-call fidelity) rather than aggregate metrics alone.
- Intended to integrate with: quant-orchestrator, shadow-eval, probe-fabric, eval-mesh, and inference-runtime.

Definitions
-----------
- Slice: a user-visible subset of traffic defined by prompt family, language, tenant, or context-length bucket.
- Quant profile: a named configuration used by the quant-orchestrator (e.g., fast-int8-v2, hybrid-fp16-int8).
- Fidelity delta: change in a quality metric (e.g., exact-match, BLEU-like score, intent-preservation) between baseline and quantized artifact.

Owner & Contacts
----------------
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (Applied ML) — maya@redwood.ai
- Runtime integration: Benji Walker (Serving Runtime) — benji@redwood.ai
- Oncall escalation: Eng-SRE rotation (see internal rota page)

Service SLOs & Risk Thresholds
-----------------------------
- Production quality SLO (global): intent-preservation >= 96% over 24h rolling.
- Slice fidelity alert: raise if fidelity delta > 2.0 percentage points for high-impact slices, > 5.0 for low-impact slices.
- Latency target: p95 <= 350ms for hosted, p95 <= 200ms for dedicated low-latency tier. Quantized artifacts should not increase p95 latency by > 15ms.
- Cost target: token cost reduction >= 18% to qualify for aggressive rollout.

Risk Matrix (slice x quant strategy)
-----------------------------------
(Use this matrix during onboarding to decide mitigation strategy. Columns are suggested mitigations.)

| Slice Type                 | Conservative (FP16) | Hybrid (FP16+INT8) | Aggressive (INT8) | Recommended Monitoring |
|---------------------------|---------------------:|-------------------:|------------------:|------------------------|
| High-sensitivity legal/compliance prompts | Allowed with canary | Shadow-only | Disallowed for first 30d | fidelity_delta, manual review |
| Function-call fidelity    | Canary + low ramp    | Shadow + probe     | Only with fallback to FP16 | function_call_exact_match, trace logs |
| Long-context >8k tokens   | FP16 default         | Progressive cache warm | INT8 only for cached prefixes | kv_cache_hit_rate, coherence_index |
| Low-frequency rare intents | Shadow only         | Auto-sample for probes | Acceptable if probe pass | slice-score, annotator-sample |
| Non-critical UI copy generation | Allowed            | Allowed            | Allowed             | brevity, style-consistency |

Onboarding checklist (quant profile promotion)
------------------------------------------------
1. Create quant artifact in a named build (e.g., modelX-hybrid-20260209).
2. Run full eval-mesh: automated slice probes + annotator checks (minimum 10k probe budget per major language).
3. Validate shadow-eval pass: no slice with fidelity_delta > thresholds above for 72h of shadow traffic.
4. Smoke test in canary: route 0.5% live traffic for 24h, collect metrics.
5. If canary passes, ramp to 5% for 48h, then to 25% for 72h. Maintain SLI checks at each stage.
6. Final promotion: if no slice alerts and cost target met, promote to 100% routing or to dedicated pools per capacity policy.

Canary & Shadow Policies
------------------------
- Shadow-eval: run quant artifact in parallel to baseline for 14 days for high-impact customers; collect telemetry but do not serve responses.
- Canary windows: default ramp schedule (0.5% -> 5% -> 25%). For high-sensitivity slices require slower ramps (0.1% -> 1% -> 5%).
- Fallthrough fallback: every request receives a hashed fallback key; if slice fidelity alert triggers, all traffic for that slice is rerouted to FP16 baseline within 5 minutes via smart-routing.

Telemetry & Alerts
------------------
Required telemetry emitted by inference-runtime when serving a quant artifact:
- model_artifact (string) e.g., modelX-hybrid-20260209
- quant_profile (string) e.g., hybrid-fp16-int8-v3
- slice_id (string) — derived by probe-fabric classification
- fidelity_delta_pct (float as string)
- latency_ms_p95 (int as string)
- kv_cache_hit_rate_pct (int as string)

Alert rules (examples):
1) slice-fidelity-major: fidelity_delta_pct > 2.0 for slice.label in ["legal","financial","function-call"] sustained for 30m -> P1 alert to Applied ML + SRE.
2) quant-latency-regress: latency_ms_p95 increase > 20ms over baseline for 15m -> P2 alert to Serving Runtime.
3) probe-failure-rate: automated probe sample pass rate < 90% over 1h -> P1 runbook.

Example alert config (YAML)
--------------------------
monitoring_rule: |
  name: slice-fidelity-major
  selector: quant_profile=~".*(int8|hybrid).*"
  expr: fidelity_delta_pct{slice=~"(legal|financial|function-call)"} > 2.0
  for: 30m
  severity: P1
  notify: ["applied-ml","eng-sre","serving-runtime"]

Diagnostics & Triage Playbook
----------------------------
1. Triage kickoff (first 15min): collect run_id, model_artifact, quant_profile, slice_id, recent probe_ids, and affected tenant ids.
2. Reproduce locally: use eval-mesh to replay failing probes against baseline and quant artifact. If failing in shadow but not locally, capture network/telemetry traces.
3. Fast rollback: trigger smart-routing fallback for slice to baseline artifact (documented CLI below). Notify stakeholders.
4. Deep analysis: run perturbation suite (prompt mutations, context length variation, random seeds) to isolate failure mode.
5. Remediation options: tighten quant profile, increase precision on sensitive layers, apply per-slice routing to baseline, or annotate probe set and initiate re-quant cycle.

Operational Commands
--------------------
- Promote artifact: rcli quant promote --artifact modelX-hybrid-20260209 --profile hybrid-fp16-int8-v3 --team applied-ml
- Start shadow run: rcli eval shadow-start --artifact modelX-hybrid-20260209 --buckets legal,function-call,long-context --duration 14d
- Emergency fallback for slice: rcli routing set-fallback --slice-id function-call --target modelX-fp16-20251201 --reason "slice-fidelity-major"

Per-slice mitigation catalog (examples)
-------------------------------------
- Fallback routing: instant reroute to baseline for the slice.
- Layer-level FP16 pinning: keep first and last N transformer layers in FP16, quantize middle layers.
- Prefetch KV warmup: for long-context slices, warm KV and use hybrid cache-aware quant path.
- Annotator audit: human review for functional regressions on function-call outputs.

Governance & Approval
---------------------
- Small changes (profile parameter tweaks) require applied-ml owner + serving-runtime reviewer.
- Medium changes (new quant profile) require Applied ML sign-off and a 72h shadow-eval pass.
- High-impact changes (customer-facing legal/financial slices) require Product and Security review and a 14-day shadow period.

Appendix: Example eval-mesh job spec (JSON as string payload)
-----------------------------------------------------------
{
  "job_name": "quant-slice-eval-20260209",
  "artifact": "modelX-hybrid-20260209",
  "slices": ["function-call","legal","long-context-16k"],
  "probes_per_slice": 12000,
  "annotations": true,
  "seeds": [42, 97, 2026]
}

Notes & Rationale
-----------------
- Per-slice decisioning reduces false positives from aggregate metrics and allows targeted remediation without throwing away global cost wins.
- Hybrid strategies (layer pinning, cache-aware quant paths) often capture most cost benefits while preserving critical behaviors.
- The thresholds above reflect historical regressions observed in 2025 shadow experiments and are subject to annual review.

Related artifacts & further reading
----------------------------------
- See internal library: quant-orchestrator API spec and quant-profile repository.
- Reference: model decomposition for serving-aware-evals (internal) for instructions on creating slice probes.
